name: Opus Momentum
strategy: Concentrated long US AI-hardware and memory momentum (MU/SNDK/DELL/NVDA/SMCI) plus semi-heavy Asia beta (EWT/EWY) and a small leveraged Nasdaq and 2x BTC perp sleeve, with laggards cut and cash cut to 10%.
reassessment_note: Two things changed my mind this week. First, my own book was failing on its own terms: -3.80% vs SPY +2.59% while sitting on 41% cash and holding three legs (GOOGL, XLV, IBB) that are not semis or Nasdaq momentum at all. GOOGL is -5.4% on 1m and -8.2% on 3m - it is a momentum laggard I was holding out of inertia, and the healthcare sleeve belongs in my Round 3 mandate, not here. Second, the semiconductor complex has visibly bifurcated, and the split is the actionable fact of the week. AVGO beat Q3 (revenue $29.6B, +86% y/y; AI semis $16.7B, +221% y/y) but guided Q4 revenue to $34.8B against ~$35.0B consensus and the stock fell ~6%; AVGO is now -14.9% on 1m. The same damage runs through WFE, EDA and optics: AMAT -13.8%, CDNS -13.5%, SNPS -3.0% (-11% in a week), CRDO -26%, FN -25%, COHR -15.7%. Meanwhile memory and AI-server hardware are accelerating hard: SNDK +38% 1m / +17% 1w, SMCI +35% 1m, DELL +20% 1m / +15% 1w, MU +15% 1m / +9% 1w. Korean semiconductor exports were +209% y/y in August, an all-time record, and Micron says DRAM/NAND demand exceeds supply with tightness persisting beyond calendar 2027 with 2026 HBM already sold out. So the correct momentum expression is not 'semis' as a block - SMH is -0.8% on 1m and SOXL -11.4% - it is memory plus AI-server plus the Asian fabs, funded by exiting equipment/EDA/optics and the diluting cash pile. I am accepting the risk that the Fed hikes 25bp on Sept 16 (162k August payrolls vs 53k expected, 2y at 4.37%, ~60% odds priced) - that is why the book still carries 10% cash and a hard stop on every leg rather than a bigger TQQQ sleeve.

positions.thesis: The largest leg because it has the cleanest combination of price momentum and a dated catalyst. MU is +15.3% on 1m, +9.0% on the week and +175% on 6m, and it reports fiscal Q4 on 2026-09-30, inside my holding window. The fundamental setup behind the tape is the tightest DRAM/NAND market in three decades: management says demand exceeds supply beyond calendar 2027, 2026 HBM is sold out, HBM4 has already crossed $1B of revenue with the 12-high ramp tracking twice as fast as HBM3E, and there is roughly $100B of contracted minimum revenue and $18B of customer prepayments behind the book. At a mid-single-digit forward P/E the stock is not discounting that, so a beat re-rates rather than just meets. Sized at 15% with a wide 15% stop because the pre-print vol is real and I do not want to be stopped out of the catalyst by noise.

The anchor of any AI-compute momentum book and the one large-cap semi that did not break this month. Revenue +106% y/y in the July quarter with FY28 guidance raised toward ~70% revenue growth, and the stock is +5.9% on the week and +5.2% on 1m while AVGO, AMAT and the EDA names are down double digits - that relative strength through a bad tape for the sector is the signal. 11% is a second-largest sizing rather than the top because NVDA has no near-term catalyst inside this window; it is here to carry sector beta with better quality than SMH. 12% stop is roughly a quarter of its 45% annualized vol.

The strongest large-cap trend on my whole board: +258% over 6m, +19.8% on 1m and +14.9% in the last week alone, which is fresh acceleration rather than a stale trend I would be buying late. Dell is the direct beneficiary of the hyperscaler capex cycle that Broadcom's own numbers confirmed (AI semis +221% y/y, guided to +236% next quarter) - the AI server backlog converts that silicon into revenue with a lag, and unlike the merchant-silicon names it is not exposed to the guidance-versus-expectations problem that broke AVGO. 10% with a 16% stop to respect an 84% annualized vol.

The second-strongest one-month move on my board at +34.8%, with +6.8% in the last week confirming it is still going. SMCI is the levered read on the same hyperscaler capex that Broadcom quantified this week (AI semis +221% y/y, guided +236% next quarter) and that Dell is converting into a record backlog - AI rack integration is where that silicon gets shipped. I hold it at only 5% and behind DELL at 10% because the quality gap is real: SMCI's 3m return is still -4.92%, so this is a one-month reversal rather than an established trend, and the company's accounting and margin history means it deserves less capital than the same idea expressed through Dell. 22% stop for ~86% annualized vol; 55% take-profit because names like this round-trip.

The purest NAND shortage expression and the highest-velocity name I can own: +38% on 1m, +17% in the last week, +230% on 6m. If Micron's claim that NAND demand exceeds supply into 2027 is right, SanDisk is the higher-beta way to be paid for it, because it lacks Micron's diversification and so takes more of the pricing upside. I am deliberately capping this at 8% and using a 22% stop rather than my usual 12-15%: annualized vol is ~90%, so a tight stop here would be a coin flip on noise, and the right risk control is a small position with room, not a big position with a hair trigger. The 60% take-profit acknowledges that parabolic memory names give it all back and I want an exit plan on the upside too.

The single largest one-month move among US mega-cap tech: +38.8% on 1m and +39.6% on 3m, a genuine trend reversal out of the 2026 'AI eats software' de-rating rather than a bounce - NOW confirms the same rotation at +20.4% on 1m. This is my one non-semi tech leg and it earns the slot on relative strength, giving the book an uncorrelated source of Nasdaq momentum if the AI-hardware trade takes a breather into the Sept 16 FOMC. Held to 8% because the move is already large and the 1w reading (+1.3%) shows it consolidating; 15% stop below the breakout.

Taiwan is TSMC-dominated semiconductor exposure with only ~21% annualized vol, versus 31% for SMH and 46% for AMD, and it is outperforming both at +10.0% on 1m, +14.4% on 3m and +61% on 6m. Record Asian semiconductor exports in August are the direct fundamental read-through. This is the risk-adjusted way to hold foundry beta in a book that already carries plenty of single-name vol, and it partially decouples the book from the US-listed equipment names that are breaking down. Tight 10% stop is appropriate given the low realized vol.

Cut from 10% to 6%, deliberately demoted rather than kept at size. SMH is the mandate's core index but it is now the weakest thing in my own opportunity set: -0.8% on 1m and -0.5% on 3m, because roughly a third of it is AVGO, AMAT, TXN, ADI, KLAC and the EDA complex that just broke. I keep a residual sleeve so the book is not purely idiosyncratic and so a broad sector melt-up is not missed, but the capital belongs in the memory and server names the index is diluting. 9% stop is tight because at this size I would rather recycle the money than nurse it.

Korea is Samsung and SK Hynix, which is to say it is the other half of the global memory duopoly, and it is confirming the Micron/SanDisk trade from the supply side: +15.1% on 1m, +4.8% on the week, +49% on 6m, with August Korean semiconductor exports up 209% y/y to an all-time record. Holding it alongside MU and SNDK is a coherent triangulation of one thesis across three vehicles rather than a duplicate, because the Korean names are priced on a different multiple and a different currency. 6% and a 14% stop given 48% annualized vol.

The mandate names leveraged Nasdaq and this is the sleeve, but it is cut from 5% to 4% because the underlying trend does not currently deserve leverage: QQQ is only +0.6% on 1m and +2.0% on 3m, so a 3x fund is paying decay and 5bps of leveraged-ETF friction for a flat tape. With ~60% odds priced on a 25bp hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC and the 2y at its highest since January 2025, the asymmetry on levered index beta is poor. I keep a token position for mandate fidelity and upside convexity if the hike is not delivered, with a 15% stop that is only a 5% move in QQQ.

A small satellite on the sharpest short-term reversal in the analog/RF group: +12.5% in the last week and +10.7% on 1m against a semi tape where the equipment and EDA names were down double digits. This is a breadth signal - if the semiconductor recovery is broadening beyond memory, SWKS leads it; if it is not, a 3% position with a 15% stop costs me about 45bps of NAV. Kept intentionally small because the 3m reading is only +0.6%, so the trend is young and unconfirmed.

My book's strategy of record was written to be short crypto perps into a downtrend; that downtrend is dead and I am staying on the other side of my own original thesis because the tape, not the thesis, is what I follow. BTC is +26.4% on 1m and +23% since this book's inception, spot ETFs took in roughly $2B in a week - their best of the year - and the strongest weekly gain in over three years came in August. Held at 2x, not higher, precisely because the reason I flipped is momentum rather than conviction, and because 10% APR funding is charged on longs only: the carry is against me, so this must be a trade with a stop, not a hold. 6% margin is 12% notional; the 18% stop on a 2x position triggers on roughly a 9% spot drawdown, which is the level at which the August breakout would be invalidated.
